# MediaForge

> MediaForge is a free, open-source media converter that runs on the user's own computer. Paste a video link or choose a local file, pick a format, and download the result as MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV, FLAC, OGG, Opus, MP4, WebM or MKV. It is a local web app (FastAPI, yt-dlp, FFmpeg, plain HTML/CSS/JS) with a Windows app that needs no Python. MIT licensed, made by Alwin as a learning and portfolio project.

Key facts:
- Cost: free, no account, no ads. Files are processed on the user's computer.
- Platforms: Windows 10/11 app (zip, no installer); Docker or Python 3.10+ on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- Inputs: links from any site yt-dlp supports, playlists, and local audio or video files.
- Extras: volume, trim, subtitles, sponsor-segment skipping, chapter splitting, target file size, and spatial sound for headphones (orbit, front, back, sides, room, movie-style surround).
- Not a hosted service. It is meant to run locally. Users are responsible for having the right to download and convert the content they use.
